abort.already_in_progress: Setup for this device is already in progress
abort.no_devices_found:
No BUSY Bar devices found.
Make sure to check the following:
- BUSY Bar is charged and powered on
- The HTTP API is on: SETTINGS > Wi-Fi on the bar
- If you want to use Wi-Fi, go to SETTINGS > Wi-Fi and check whether BUSY Bar is connected to the same network than the machine running Home Assistant.
- If you want to use USB, check whether BUSY Bar is connected to the machine running Home Assistant.
abort.http_api_disabled:
{name} was found on the network but did not answer over HTTP.
A bar keeps announcing itself even with its HTTP API turned off, which is why it appears here and then cannot be added.
On the bar, open SETTINGS > Wi-Fi and turn on the HTTP API, then add it again. If the API is already on, the bar may have been busy - try once more.

zeroconf_confirm.description: Do you want to set up {name}?

mint_token.description: The bar's HTTP API over Wi-Fi has to be on for Home Assistant to reach it. If the API asks for an access key, enter it; the key is shown on the bar under SETTINGS > Wi-Fi.

device_unreachable.message: The bar is no longer answering. Check its Wi-Fi or USB connection, and that its HTTP API is still turned on.

access_unauthorized.message: Device has been removed from this smart home. Please reconfigure the device.

unknown_device.message: That device is not known to Home Assistant.

device_not_loaded.message: The BUSY Bar for that device is not set up.

feature_needs_newer_firmware.message: {feature} needs BUSY Bar API {required_version}; this bar reports {device_version}. Update the firmware.

no_firmware_to_install.message: The bar has not reported a firmware version to install.

firmware_install_failed.message: Could not start the firmware update: {error}

input_failed.message: The bar did not accept that input: {error}

timer_not_running.message: No session is running on the bar, so there is nothing to change: {error}

timer_failed.message: The bar did not accept that change: {error}

unknown_theme.message: This bar has no theme called {theme}. It has: {available}.

phase_too_short.message: The bar will not run a session of that length: {error}

file_not_allowed.message: Home Assistant is not allowed to read {file}. Put the file under its `www` folder or a media folder, or add the folder to `allowlist_external_dirs`.

file_not_convertible.message: {file} cannot be converted for the bar: {error}

upload_failed.message: The bar did not take the file: {error}

session_owns_the_screen.message: {bar} is running a session, and a session refuses every drawing while it lasts - there is no priority that gets past it. End the session, or let it finish.

screen_is_busy.message: {bar} is showing something of its own and refused an ordinary notification. Turn on “Show it over other drawings” to put this one above it.

unknown_asset.message: This bar has no {kind} called {name}. It has {count} of them - run the “List what a bar can show and play” action to see which.

upload_would_be_replaced.message: Taking {name} from {application} would write over a file of your own under the same name. Name yours as {own}, or upload theirs under a different name.

unknown_asset_closest.message: This bar has no {kind} called {name}. The closest it has: {closest}. Run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for all {count}.

notify.name: Show a notification
notify.description: Shows a message on the bar's front display, laid out to fit, with an optional icon and sound.

line_1.name: Line 1
line_1.description: The first, or only, line of text.

line_2.name: Line 2
line_2.description: A second line. Giving it uses the two-line layout.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: The icon drawn at the left edge, by name. To see what this bar has, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set. A bare name is read as your own upload first and then as one the firmware ships; write `draw_tool/logo` - or `draw_tool/logo.png` - to mean a file another app uploaded, which is copied into Home Assistant's folder the first time you name it.

sound.name: Sound
sound.description: A sound to play with the notification; leave it empty for silence. To hear what this bar has, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set. Names work as for the icon: your own upload wins a bare name, and `app_name/sound` says which folder you mean.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long the notification stays on screen.

font.name: First line size
font.description: How big the first line is - and the second too, unless that one is given a size of its own. The two tallest sizes are for a single line: two lines do not fit them.

background_color.name: Background colour
background_color.description: Fills the panel behind the text. Needs API 24.3.0.

font_2.name: Second line size
font_2.description: A size for the second line alone. A label over a detail - big over tiny - says which of the two matters, where one size for both says they are equal.

interrupt.name: Show it over other drawings
interrupt.description: Puts this notification above whatever else is drawn on the bar by an app. It does not get past a running session: the firmware refuses every drawing while one is on.

start_busy.name: Start the BUSY card
start_busy.description: Starts the session the card in the BUSY switch position describes - the same thing the bar's own switch starts.

theme.name: Theme
theme.description: Show this session in a theme of your choosing. Nothing on the bar is changed: the card keeps its own theme, which the bar returns to when the session ends. To see the themes this bar has, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set.

start_custom.name: Start the CUSTOM card
start_custom.description: Starts the session the card in the CUSTOM switch position describes.

theme.name: Theme
theme.description: Show this session in a theme of your choosing. Nothing on the bar is changed: the card keeps its own theme, which the bar returns to when the session ends. To see the themes this bar has, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set.

start_quick_infinite.name: Start a quick infinite session
start_quick_infinite.description: Runs with no end, until it is stopped. Neither of the bar's cards is written or even named: a quick session carries its own settings and names a card outside both switch positions, which is what the BUSY app shows it under.

theme.name: Theme
theme.description: How this session looks on the bar. Left out, the theme configured for this kind of quick session is used. To see the themes this bar has, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set.

start_quick_simple.name: Start a quick countdown
start_quick_simple.description: Runs for a given number of minutes, then ends. Neither of the bar's cards is written or even named.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How many minutes to run, up to 24 hours. There is no minimum - the firmware checks a countdown only at the top. Left out, the configured quick countdown length is used.

theme.name: Theme
theme.description: How this session looks on the bar. Left out, the theme configured for this kind of quick session is used. To see the themes this bar has, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set.

start_quick_interval.name: Start a quick interval session
start_quick_interval.description: Runs work and rest phases in turn. Neither of the bar's cards is written or even named.

work.name: Work
work.description: Minutes of work in each phase, 5 minutes to 8 hours. Left out, the configured value is used.

rest.name: Rest
rest.description: Minutes of rest between work phases, 5 minutes to 8 hours - the bar refuses anything shorter, so a 5/1 session is not possible.

cycles.name: Cycles
cycles.description: How many work phases to run, between 2 and 35.

theme.name: Theme
theme.description: How this session looks on the bar. Left out, the theme configured for this kind of quick session is used. To see the themes this bar has, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set.

next_phase.name: Skip to the next phase
next_phase.description: Moves an interval session on: work becomes rest, rest becomes the next work. After the last interval the session ends.

set_theme.name: Set the theme
set_theme.description: Changes the theme. Without a card, the running session changes and reverts when it ends; with one, that card's own theme changes for good.

theme.name: Theme
theme.description: A theme this bar has. The bar's own list is on its theme entities; a name it does not have is refused rather than stored. To see them, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Change this mode's own theme instead of the running session's.

play_sound.name: Play a sound
play_sound.description: Plays one of the bar's built-in sounds.

sound.name: Sound
sound.description: Which sound to play - any the bar has, the timer's own included. To see them, run the “List what a bar can show and play” action for this bar's own set.

clear.name: Clear the display
clear.description: Removes what this integration drew, leaving the bar's own screen. Notifications with a duration disappear on their own.

stop_session.name: End the session
stop_session.description: Ends the session, leaving nothing running. Not the same as the selector's off position, which is the bar's do-not-disturb.

pause_session.name: Pause the session
pause_session.description: Pauses the running session where it is.

list_assets.name: List what a bar can show and play
list_assets.description: Answers with the icons, animations, sounds, fonts and themes this bar holds - the firmware's own and anything uploaded to it, which no fixed list can know. Every name comes back written the way a field takes it, so the answer can be read straight into an automation. The whole set is pictured in the documentation, linked from this integration's page.

upload_asset.name: Put a picture or sound of your own on a bar
upload_asset.description: Uploads a file from this Home Assistant to the bar, converted for it on the way, and answers with the name to use. That name is then what the icon and sound fields take. A file uploaded by the BUSY app or the Draw Tool cannot be used from here: the bar keeps each application's uploads apart, and only reaches its own.

file.name: File
file.description: Path to the file on the machine Home Assistant runs on. It has to be somewhere Home Assistant is allowed to read - `/config/www` and the media folders are, by default. A picture is scaled to the panel and a sound re-encoded for the speaker.

name.name: Name on the bar
name.description: What to call it there. Defaults to the file's own name; an icon wider than the panel is refused when it is used, so keep pictures small.
